title: Tail-latency-focused load orchestrator and acceptance protocol for Dedicated capacity
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines and implements a tail-latency-first load testing harness, a reproducible benchmarking methodology, and a customer-facing acceptance protocol for Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees and autoscaling policies. The goal is to produce deterministic measurements that validate latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99), throughput headroom, and autoscaler behavior under realistic multi-tenant traffic patterns so Sales/Customer Engineering can sign Dedicated capacity purchases with clear guarantees.

Goals:
- Build a configurable load orchestrator that stresses tail latencies across sequence lengths, KV cache states (cold/warm), and request heterogeneity.
- Define an immutable benchmarking methodology and artifact set: traffic mixes, warmup routines, sampling windows, and noise controls.
- Produce a customer acceptance checklist and automated report generator (CSV + HTML) that maps observed metrics to contractable guarantees.
- Validate autoscaling triggers and cooldowns (scale-up/scale-down) under representative burst patterns.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change runtime scheduling or kernel code. It will produce observability artifacts and recommend runtime config changes in follow-ups.

Success criteria / Acceptance criteria:
- The harness can run a canonical throughput test that reproduces p99 latency within ±10% across repeated runs on the same fleet image.
- Benchmark run produces: throughput (tokens/sec), p50/p95/p99 latencies, GPU utilization, autoscaler events timeline, and KV cache hit-rate.
- Customer acceptance doc produced and validated in 2 pilot runs with an internal beta customer.
- Test artifacts and a one-click runbook (GitHub Actions) exist for QA and on-call to reproduce failures.

Metrics to collect and how to compute them:
- Throughput: total tokens served / steady-state window duration (tokens/sec). Report per-model and combined.
- Latency (ms): per-request end-to-end wall-clock; report p50/p95/p99 over steady-state windows and over the full run.
- Tail-latency drift: percent difference of p99 between runs.
- Autoscaler stability: count of scale events / minute, mean time between scale decisions.
- Cold-start penalty: latency delta for requests where KV cache not yet populated for a prefix.

Harness design (high level):
- Controller: single orchestrator that schedules traffic generators across multiple runner nodes (GCE/EC2 or k8s jobs).
- Load generators: Golang-based HTTP prober that supports per-client concurrency, adjustable token generation rate, sequence length profiles, and synthetic user think-times.
- Traffic profiles: JSON recipes describing mix of short/medium/long sequences, embedding-only calls, streaming vs non-streaming, and multi-tenant routing.
- KV cache warmers: optional pre-seed phase that simulates typical prefix distributions to reach desired cache hit rates.
- Observability hooks: Prometheus exporters, per-request tracing IDs, and sample payload dump.
- Report generator: script to aggregate logs, compute metrics, and emit an HTML acceptance report + CSV artifact.

Benchmarking methodology (immutable steps):
1) Fleet prep: deploy the target runtime image, ensure telemetry endpoints are enabled, and confirm autoscaler policies are set to the target config.
2) Baseline warmup: run cache warmer and low-rate traffic for 10 minutes to stabilize kernel/JIT caches.
3) Ramp-in: increase load gradually over 5-15 minutes to target throughput to observe autoscaler behavior, then hold steady for a configurable steady-state window (default 10 minutes).
4) Burst tests: run 1-minute bursts at 3-5x steady throughput to validate scale-up times and tail-latency impact.
5) Scale-down observation: after stopping bursts, observe scale-down and ensure no oscillations beyond defined thresholds.
6) Repeatability: run the canonical test 3 times. Compute mean and variance for p99.
7) Artifact capture: export raw traces, aggregated PM metrics, GPU metrics, and the final acceptance report to the run artifact storage (GCS/Drive link).

Customer acceptance tests and checklist (for Sales/CE sign-off):
- Preconditions: fleet image hash, autoscaler policy, and model version pinned.
- Run canonical test in customer's Dedicated staging account (or sandbox) with CE present.
- Verify p99 <= contract SLO during steady-state window.
- Verify throughput >= committed tokens/sec and autoscaler adheres to the agreed scale-up cooldown.
- Confirm KV cache hit-rate >= expected threshold for workload profile or document expected cold-start grace.
- Validate graceful fallback behavior: when model variant unavailable, traffic routed to compatible variant within latency budget.
- Sign-off captured in the HTML report and an emailed artifact with run ID and GitHub actions link.

Deliverables:
- Load orchestrator binaries and recipes (GitHub repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dedicated-load-orch - PR TBD).
- Immutable benchmarking playbook (Confluence: https://confluence.company.com/display/DED/Throughput+Playbook).
- Automated acceptance-report generator and GitHub Action workflow.
- Customer-facing acceptance checklist and runbook document.

Risk & mitigations:
- Risk: noisy infra on shared clouds creates run variance. Mitigation: recommend running in reserved infra nodes (Dedicated test pools) and include noise-detection heuristics.
- Risk: autoscaler flapping during scale-down. Mitigation: include cooldown enforcement tests and explicit thresholds in the acceptance checklist.

Prereqs / infra tickets:
- Ensure Dedicated test pool is provisioned and network ACLs allow traffic generator access. (Infra ticket: INF-2125)
- Telemetry retention increase to 7 days for run artifact analysis (Infra ticket: OBS-781).

Notes / links:
- See related capacity tooling tickets: ENG-63421 (acceptance-profiles), ENG-42199 (e2e-load-framework).
- Draft PR for the orchestrator: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dedicated-load-orch/pull/12 (WIP).

Next steps:
- Finalize load profiles and schedule the first internal pilot run with CE week of 2025-11-24.
- Create GitHub Actions workflow for canonical test runs and artifact upload.
- Iterate with runtime team on recommended config changes after initial measurements.
